encounters.cc: Progressive darkening and thickening of skin in her axillae and around the neck for 6 months

lines: Progressive darkening and thickening of skin in her axillae and around the neck for 6 months
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of progressive darkening and thickening of the skin in her axillae and around the neck.
She reports no itching or pain associated with these areas.
Her past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is poorly controlled on metformin, and hypertension.
She denies any family history of cancer.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Data entry specialist.
Her body mass index (BMI) is 35 kg/m^2.
On physical examination, symmetrical, hyperpigmented, velvety plaques are noted in the axilla and around the neck.

encounters.cc: Progressive pain in right knee worse with activity and improving with rest over 3 months

lines: Progressive pain in right knee worse with activity and improving with rest over 3 months
The patient with diabetes and prior acanthosis nigricans presents with knee pain.
She reports pain worse with activity and improves with rest, denying recent trauma or injury.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Data entry specialist.
Her body mass index is 34 kg/m^2
On examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the medial aspect of the tibial condyle, without erythema or warmth.
The range of motion of the knee is preserved, but she experiences pain with resisted knee flexion.
An x-ray of the knee shows mild joint space narrowing without evidence of fracture.

encounters.cc: Burning pain and tingling in left foot worse at night and after prolonged standing for 3 months

lines: Burning pain and tingling in left foot worse at night and after prolonged standing for 3 months
The patient with type 2 diabetes returns to Orthopedics following knee evaluation.
She notes that the symptoms are worse at night and after prolonged periods of standing.
She denies any recent trauma or injury to the foot.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Data entry specialist.
On physical examination, there is no erythema or swelling, but she has a positive Tinel sign at the medial malleolus.
Dorsiflexion of the foot exacerbates the pain.
Her most recent laboratory values are as follows:

encounters.cc: Mild right-sided abdominal discomfort ongoing for several weeks with no nausea or weight loss

lines: Mild right-sided abdominal discomfort ongoing for several weeks with no nausea or weight loss

This 52-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity presents with several weeks of mild right-sided abdominal discomfort following recent encounters for acanthosis nigricans, pes anserinus pain syndrome, and tarsal tunnel syndrome.
She denies nausea, vomiting, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits.
She has a history of type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia, both of which are suboptimally controlled.
She takes metformin and a statin but has not seen her endocrinologist in over a year.
She does not smoke or consume alcohol.
She reports being mostly sedentary and admits to irregular dietary habits.
Vitals: Temperature 98.4°F (36.9°C), Blood Pressure 142/90 mmHg, Pulse 82/min, Respiratory Rate 16/min.
Physical examination shows mild hepatomegaly without tenderness.
No stigmata of chronic liver disease are noted.

encounters.cc: Irregular, heavy menstrual bleeding with unpredictable cycles and intermenstrual spotting for 6 months

lines: Irregular, heavy menstrual bleeding with unpredictable cycles and intermenstrual spotting for 6 months

This 53-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity, previously evaluated for acanthosis nigricans and hepatic steatosis, presents to the Obstetrics & Gynecology clinic with a 6-month history of irregular, heavy menstrual bleeding.
She reports that her menstrual cycles used to be regular, with moderate flow lasting 5 days, but they have become unpredictable, with episodes of spotting between periods.
She has not had a menstrual period for the past 2 months.
Her past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension.
Her most recent Pap smear was normal.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Data entry specialist.
She has a BMI of 35 kg/m^2. her blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg
On physical examination, a bimanual pelvic exam reveals an enlarged, nontender uterus.
Total cholesterol: 220 mg/dL (Normal: 50 mg/dL in women)

encounters.cc: Fatigue and right upper quadrant discomfort persistent for 6 months

lines: Fatigue and right upper quadrant discomfort persistent for 6 months
The patient is a 54-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity who returns to the Gastroenterology clinic following prior evaluation for right upper quadrant discomfort in 2020.
She presents with a 6-month history of fatigue and right upper quadrant discomfort.
Her medications include metformin and lisinopril
She denies any history of alcohol use
On physical examination, her BMI is 32 kg/m^2, and she has hepatomegaly without jaundice, ascites, or spider angiomata
Abdominal ultrasonography shows increased echogenicity of the liver consistent with hepatic steatosis.
There is no evidence of gallstones or biliary ductal dilatation

encounters.cc: Requesting copy of medical records for transfer of care to new provider in another state

lines: Requesting copy of medical records for transfer of care to new provider in another state
This 55-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity, previously evaluated for acanthosis nigricans, returns for care transfer.
She reports moving to another state and wishes to transfer her care to a new provider, inquiring about the process and timeline for obtaining her medical records.
She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia.
Her current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Data entry specialist.
On examination, her blood pressure is 132/86 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and BMI is 31 kg/m^2.
Her most recent laboratory results are as follows:

encounters.cc: Worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for 2 days following recent procedure

lines: Worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for 2 days following recent procedure

This 56-year-old female with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and history of chronic abdominal discomfort presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.
She underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy 5 days ago.
Her past medical history is significant for obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Data entry specialist.
On examination, her temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), heart rate is 110 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg.
Abdominal examination reveals diffuse tenderness with guarding, but no rebound tenderness.
An abdominal CT scan with oral contrast is performed.
